author: agent:claude-code
message: The user kept today's behavior: removing an observed node or edge takes its props with it, stated ones included. The rule now says what the code and the pinned test do. Also Forest's mark_with_ancestors (parda's graft 01a10a6b, point 6) and the follow-ups that graft names. (proposal 01a10ac9-624f-7743-ac3b-776eb11afb68, proposed by agent:claude-code, accepted by user)

text: An observation never overwrites a stated fact, or removes a stated node or edge; removing an observed node or edge takes its props with it, stated ones included.

title: Removing an observed node takes its stated props with it
body: When a scanner no longer sees what it observed, the node or edge goes, and what a person stated about it goes too; the log keeps it, so it can be restored. Protecting such nodes would leave ghosts of vanished machines, contradict the behavior pinned since Alfred (stated_facts_survive_observations), and turn removals already in Alfred's log and every .tend/log into conflicts on replay, since op JSON is stored data.

reason: Decided to keep the behavior: removing an observed node takes its stated props with it (see the decision on Property graphs); the rule is reworded to say so.

title: mark_with_ancestors, for dirty walks
body: Marks a node and its ancestors in a Column<bool>, stopping at the first one already marked: O(depth) for the first mark on a path, O(1) amortized over a pass. Asked by parda (graft 01a10a6b, point 6), since every incremental pass needs it.

title: Flat::update: patch the changed subtree's range instead of rebuilding
body: Today a rebuild is O(n) (42 us at 10k, 422 us at 100k) whenever Forest::version moved. Fine while structure changes only after reconciliation; patching just the moved or changed subtree's range would cut it. From parda's graft 01a10a6b, point 3.

title: Forest: a bulk append_children(parent, n), for reconciliation
body: Inserting a run of rows links each one separately; a bulk append would allocate n slots and link them in one pass. One of parda's ideas for the build gap (graft 01a10a6b, point 4), along with folding the generation into the links record, which its own measurements found slows link walks (17.6 vs 13.4 us at 10k).
